diagnostic_evidence.quote: the sequence \( \{U_h^n(\mathbf{x})\}_{n=0}^{N}\subset H_0(\Omega)\) is called a set of SLDG numerical solutions
the existence and uniqueness of the numerical solution for CSLDG, as well as the numerical stability of this scheme,

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract, introduction and conclusion claim existence, uniqueness and stability of the CSLDG (DG) numerical solution. However, Definition def-NumSol-SLDG, on which Theorems thm-NumericalScheme-Existence, thm-NumericalSolution-Stability and thm-NumericalSolution-Uniqueness are based, takes the unknown in H_0(Omega) (an L^2 space) and tests against all of H_0(Omega_K), both infinite-dimensional; no piecewise-polynomial space of degree P, quadrature, or any discretization parameter enters Section 3. The object analysed is thus a time-discrete, space-continuous transport update (U^{n+1}_K is simply the Riesz representer of the push-forward), not the P-th order DG scheme described in Section 2.2. Nothing in the paper establishes existence/uniqueness/stability for the actual DG scheme with finite-dimensional trial/test spaces.

failure_location.quote: First, the existence and uniqueness of the CSLDG numerical solutions are proven, along with the stability of the numerical scheme.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate Definition def-NumSol-SLDG with the finite-dimensional DG space V_h (piecewise polynomials of degree P) as trial and test space and re-derive the three theorems for that scheme (existence/uniqueness from invertibility of the mass matrix; stability from the L^2-projection being nonexpansive plus a bound on the characteristic-flow Jacobian), or else withdraw the claim that the DG scheme has been analysed.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised contribution ('for the first time' establishing well-posedness and stability of the CSLDG scheme) is not supported; Section 3 says nothing about the DG polynomial approximation, the mesh, or the degree P.
issues.title: Existence/stability/uniqueness theorems concern an infinite-dimensional L^2 formulation, not the DG scheme
issues.why_classification: A comparable well-posedness/stability statement for the true DG scheme is obtainable with a contained argument, but the present proofs must be re-cast for a finite-dimensional space; as written the advertised guarantee is not established.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof asserts that every point of the support is a point where the function is nonzero, and that every point of the closure of the preimage set lies in the preimage set itself. Both inferences are false: the support is a closed set (the closure of the nonvanishing set, or its essential version for L^2 functions), so boundary points of the support can be zeros, and membership in a closure does not give membership in the set; moreover pointwise values of L^2 functions Psi and psi are not well defined. The correct statement (support is transported by the flow homeomorphism) is true, but the given argument does not prove it.

failure_location.quote: For all \(\mathbf{x}^* \in \operatorname{supp}\{\psi(\mathbf{x}, t^*)\}\), where \(t^* \in [t_1, t_2]\), we have \(\psi(\mathbf{x}^*, t^*) \neq 0\).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the lemma by noting that x -> x + int A ds is a homeomorphism (the characteristic flow) and that the essential support of a composition with a homeomorphism is the preimage of the essential support, avoiding pointwise evaluation.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of lemma-psi-supp is invalid as written; the conclusion remains true and later uses are unaffected once a correct proof is supplied.
issues.title: Support lemma proof treats L^2 supports pointwise and ignores closure
issues.why_classification: A short, standard replacement argument yields the same conclusion with no loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note that once \(t_1\) and \(t_2\) are fixed, \(\int_{t_1}^{t_2} \mathbf{A}(\mathbf{s}(\tau), \tau) \, \mathrm{d}\tau\) is a constant.

issues.failure_explanation: The change of variables x = x* + int_{t_1}^{t_2} A(s(tau),tau) dtau is the characteristic flow map Phi_{t_1->t_2}(x*), because s solves ds/dtau = A(s,tau) with s(t_1) = x*; the integral therefore depends on x* and is not a constant. Its Jacobian is exp(int_{t_1}^{t_2} div A(s(tau),tau) dtau), which equals 1 only for divergence-free A. Hence dx = dx* is false in general and the norms are not invariant. Counterexample (d=1): A(x,t)=x, Psi = indicator of [1,2], t_2 - t_1 = ln 2: psi(x,t_1)=Psi(2x) is the indicator of [1/2,1], so ||psi(.,t_1)||_{L^1} = 1/2 while ||Psi||_{L^1} = 1. Both lemma-psi-Rd-LP and lemma-psi-Omega-LP, whose proofs rest on the same erroneous step, are false for general C^1 A as assumed in the paper; the correct relation is a two-sided bound with constant exp(||div A||_inf |t_2-t_1|).

failure_location.quote: Considering the \(L^P\)-norm over the entire space \(\mathbb{R}^d\), the domain of integration remains unchanged as \(\mathbb{R}^d\) before and after the change of variables. Thus, we immediately obtain

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace both lemmas by the estimate e^{-c|t_2-t_1|}||Psi|| <= ||psi(.,t_1)|| <= e^{c|t_2-t_1|}||Psi|| with c = sup|div A| (or restrict to div A = 0), and propagate the constant through Lemma-f-H*, the stability constants C_k and the uniqueness argument.
issues.overall_effect: The invariance lemmas are false for non-divergence-free advection; the boundedness proof in Lemma-f-H* (hence the Riesz step in the existence theorem), the equality ||psi^0||=||Psi|| in the stability proof, and the uniqueness proof built on it all rely on the false identity. Their conclusions survive only after inserting Jacobian-dependent constants.
issues.title: L^P-norm invariance of psi along characteristics ignores the flow Jacobian (false unless div A = 0)
issues.why_classification: The exact-invariance statement must be abandoned for the advertised class of coefficients, but a recognizably comparable norm-equivalence holds and the dependent theorems are restored with modified constants via a contained calculation.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \(H_0({\color{blue}{\Omega}})\) becomes a Hilbert space with compact support on the bounded domain \({\color{blue}{\Omega}}\).
Conversely, if \(U^n_i \in H_0(\Omega_i)\), then \(\operatorname{supp}\{U^n_i\} = \Omega_i\) and \(U^n_i \in L^2(\Omega_i)\).

issues.failure_explanation: H_0(Omega) is defined by supp f compactly contained in Omega. A function with supp{U^n_i} = Omega_i (the standing assumption of the paper, eq. eq-Uh-Ui) does not have support compactly contained in the open cell Omega_i, so the proposition's claim U^n_i in H_0(Omega_i) is false under the paper's own definition, and the converse step 'U^n_i in H_0(Omega_i) implies supp = Omega_i' is likewise false. Furthermore, the set of L^2 functions with compactly contained support is not closed in L^2 (limits may have full support), so the asserted 'Hilbert space' property fails. The same inconsistency recurs in prop-Uh-tildeU-L2-Rd and in the conclusion U_h^n in H_0(Omega) with supp U_h^n = Omega in the existence theorem.

failure_location.quote:
If \(U_h^n \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)\), then under the compact support constraint, i.e., \(\operatorname{supp}\{U^n_i\} = \Omega_i\), 
  we have \(U^n_i \in H_0(\Omega_i)\) for all \(\Omega_i \in \mathcal{T}_h\).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine H_0(Omega) as {f in L^2(R^d): f = 0 a.e. outside Omega} (a closed subspace, hence Hilbert); all propositions and theorems then go through verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: Membership statements in H_0 throughout Section 3 are contradictory with the support assumptions; the test space is not a Hilbert space as defined (Riesz is actually invoked on L^2(R^d), so that step is unaffected).
issues.title: H_0(Omega) defined via compact containment is incompatible with supp = Omega_i and is not complete
issues.why_classification: A single local redefinition removes the contradiction and preserves every result and argument.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims the new implementation avoids interpolation during dimension switching. In the algorithm, the x-sweep is performed at K_y+1 fixed transverse points [Gg]^y_s, the resulting RHS data (whose y-dependence is non-polynomial since a(x,y,t) and hence psi^x depend on y) are equated to the polynomial ansatz sum_j beta_{k,j} varphi_j([Gg]^y_s), and beta is recovered by inverting the (K_y+1)x(K_y+1) collocation matrix [Phi]^y_s. Solving [beta][Phi] = RHS is exactly polynomial interpolation of the transverse dependence at the K_y+1 nodes; the same holds for the y-sweep via ([varnothing]^x_r)^{-1}. Thus interpolation (with its associated error) is performed at every dimension switch, merely written in modal form.

failure_location.quote: Therefore, no interpolation is needed during dimension switching;

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword the claim: the scheme performs transverse polynomial interpolation implicitly through the inverse collocation matrices, its advantage being that intermediate results are stored as 2D modal polynomials rather than that interpolation is avoided.
issues.overall_effect: The stated conceptual advantage over the schemes of [1,4] is overstated; the method's correctness and observed convergence are not affected, but the characterization of the algorithm is inaccurate.
issues.title: Claim that the separated-variable splitting needs no interpolation is contradicted by its own collocation step
issues.why_classification: Only the descriptive claim needs correction; no guarantee, result, or algorithmic step changes.
